Dismiss alert {{ message }} zackees / llvm-ld Public Notifications You must be signed in to change notification settings Fork 0 Star 0 bench(report): current link speed per build mode (Debug, Release+PDB, Release no-PDB, ThinLTO): overview + per-mode paired-time bar charts, light/dark; drop the history and threads line charts   #32 New issue Copy link New issue Copy link Closed #33 Closed bench(report): current link speed per build mode (Debug, Release+PDB, Release no-PDB, ThinLTO): overview + per-mode paired-time bar charts, light/dark; drop the history and threads line charts #32 #33 Copy link Description zackees opened on Sep 18, 2026 Issue body actions Problem The README and https://zackees.github.io/llvm-ld/ show two line charts that answer the wrong question. link-speedup-history.svg ( #history ) plots speedup over published runs. Nobody needs the history; we care about current performance. It currently holds two points, both labelled 2026-09-18 . link-speedup-threads.svg ( #threads ) draws lines between thread counts 1, 2 and 4, which are separate measurements, so the lines between them mean nothing. It shows only "% faster" and never how long a link takes. Most importantly, neither chart says which kind of link was measured , and only one kind is measured. tests/perf/gen_corpus.py compiles every object with -O2 -g -gcodeview and links with /debug:full /opt:ref /opt:icf . That is a Release build with a PDB. A reader cannot tell whether llvm-ld is faster for their build (Debug, Release without a PDB, LTO). The patches target PDB emission, so the answer really does differ by mode. Goal Answer "how much faster does llvm-ld link my build, right now?" from the current run only, with: one overview bar chart in the README: wall time saved per build mode, one bar per corpus size; and one detail bar chart per build mode : paired link time (stock lld vs llvm-ld) per corpus and thread count, so a reader also sees how long a link takes and how it scales with threads. Decisions (design review) Each decision has a one-line rationale; the rest of this issue is the spec that follows from them. # Decision Why D1 Four modes: debug , release-pdb , release-nopdb , thinlto (table below). They are the four combinations a Windows developer actually has: Debug, RelWithDebInfo, Release, LTO. Everything else is a flag detail (see "Rejected modes"). D2 release-nopdb is kept as an honest control and labelled as such on its chart. No PDB is produced, so the PDB-emission patches cannot apply; a visibly ~0% row proves the benchmark is not measuring noise, and would catch a regression on the non-PDB path. D3 thinlto is measured on small and medium only, at the highest thread count only, with 5 paired runs. The link runs LLVM codegen, which the patches do not touch; a large ThinLTO link is minutes per run on the hosted runner. The chart states the expected small gain and the missing corpus in words. D4 Charts encode time , not only percent: the per-mode chart draws paired bars in ms (baseline vs llvm-ld); the overview draws % less wall time with the pair's ms in the label. Bar length proportional to time is the honest encoding, and it is the only way to show "how long does a link take". Both numbers of a pair come from one run on one machine, so the no-cross-run-absolutes rule still holds. D5 Every bar carries an interquartile-range whisker ; bench.py emits q1/q3 of the paired ratios and of each side's wall samples. n=9 (or 5) medians on a shared hosted runner look more precise than they are; IQR is distribution-free and needs no new dependency. Bootstrap CIs were considered and are overkill for n=9. D6 Every panel is rendered in a light and a dark variant , embedded with / prefers-color-scheme . The current panels are opaque dark cards on GitHub's white README. is GitHub's documented mechanism; CSS media queries inside an -embedded SVG are not reliable across browsers. Colors are validated against GitHub's actual page backgrounds ( #ffffff , #0d1117 ). D7 Bars are direct-labelled (ms at every bar tip, % above every pair). A hotlinked SVG has no hover layer, so labels are the only value channel in the README; the dashboard table is the accessible twin. D8 Corpus (small/medium/large) is an ordinal blue ramp, light -> dark; stock lld is a neutral gray, llvm-ld is the accent blue; text never wears the series color. Corpus size is ordered, so a one-hue ramp shows the order; the baseline is context and the candidate is the point (emphasis form). D9 The history chart, history.jsonl and all history plumbing are removed; comparison_key stays. Requested; nothing reads the history except the chart being removed. comparison_key is cheap and still identifies the experiment in latest.json . D10 The measurement matrix (mode -> compile flags, link flags, corpora, thread policy, runs) lives in one place , tests/perf/gen_corpus.py , and the workflow consumes it via --print-matrix . Today the corpus loop and the measure loop are hand-written in YAML; with four modes and per-mode limits that would be four places to drift. Build modes Each mode is a combination of how the objects are compiled and how they are linked . All modes keep the common flags the corpus already uses: --target=x86_64-pc-windows-msvc -c -fno-exceptions -fno-rtti -ffreestanding -nostdinc -nostdinc++ -w -fms-compatibility -mno-incremental-linker-compatible for compiling, and /entry:entry /subsystem:console /nodefaultlib /brepro /machine:x64 for linking, plus /pdbaltpath:%_PDB% whenever a PDB is produced. mode id label on charts objects (added to common) link flags (added to common) PDB corpora threads runs note printed on the chart debug Debug + PDB -O0 -g -gcodeview /debug:full /opt:noref /opt:noicf yes small, medium, large 1, 2, 4 (+nproc if > 4) 9 "a Debug build: unoptimized objects, largest debug info, no linker GC or ICF" release-pdb Release + PDB -O2 -g -gcodeview /debug:full /opt:ref /opt:icf yes small, medium, large 1, 2, 4 (+nproc if > 4) 9 "RelWithDebInfo; the mode measured until now" release-nopdb Release, no PDB -O2 /opt:ref /opt:icf (no /debug ) no small, medium, large 1, 2, 4 (+nproc if > 4) 9 "control: no PDB is produced, so the PDB-emission patches cannot apply; expect ~0%" thinlto ThinLTO + PDB -O2 -g -gcodeview -flto=thin /debug:full /opt:ref /opt:icf ( /opt:lldltojobs defaults to /threads , confirmed in Driver.cpp ) yes small, medium highest only 5 "the link runs LLVM codegen, which the patches do not touch; expect a small gain. large is not measured: a 2048-module ThinLTO link is too slow for the hosted runner" Chart order is the table order. Mode ids are fixed in code ( MODES in tests/perf/gen_corpus.py , mirrored in tools/bench_report.py with a test asserting the two lists are equal). Every cell is gated on byte-identical output (EXE, plus PDB where one is produced) and self-determinism, as today. ThinLTO determinism under a fixed /threads (hence fixed /opt:lldltojobs ) and no /lldltocache is the same contract tests/tier2_corpus.ps1 already relies on ( #28 ). Rejected modes (checked against the vendored lld/COFF/Driver.cpp ) /debug:fastlink : lld warns /debug:fastlink unsupported; using /debug:full . Not a mode. /debug:ghash with -gcodeview-ghash objects: /debug:full already sets debugGHashes = true ; lld computes the hashes in-linker when there is no .debug$H . The only difference is that hashing pass, which the patches do not touch, and MSVC cl cannot emit .debug$H . /debug:noghash is the legacy path nobody should choose. Neither is measured; both are one --extra flag away in bench.py for anyone curious. /incremental : in lld it only gates rewriting the import library ( Driver.cpp , createImportLibrary ). Not a link mode. Full LTO ( -flto ): a single monolithic codegen that is mostly serial and would take minutes per link even on medium ; the answer would be the same as ThinLTO's ("the patches do not touch codegen") at several times the cost. MinGW ( ld.lld driver) modes: a different driver and corpus generator; out of scope for this issue, tracked separately if wanted. Charts Palette (validated against GitHub's page colors) role light ( #ffffff page) dark ( #0d1117 page) background rect #ffffff #0d1117 plot area #f6f8fa #161b22 grid / axis hairline (1px, solid) #d0d7de #30363d title / value labels #1f2328 #e6edf3 muted (subtitles, axis text, footer) #59636e #8b949e stock lld bar (baseline, de-emphasis) #7a7a76 (4.3:1) #6e7681 (4.1:1) llvm-ld bar (accent) #2a78d6 (4.4:1) #3987e5 (5.2:1) corpus ramp small / medium / large (ordinal) #86b6ef / #3987e5 / #1c5cab (2.1 / 3.6 / 6.6:1; OKLab L .76 / .62 / .48) #9ec5f4 / #5598e7 / #256abf (10.6 / 6.3 / 3.5:1; L .81 / .67 / .53) Marks: bars at most 24px wide, 4px rounded data end, square at the baseline, 2px surface gap between adjacent bars; whiskers 1px in the muted color with 4px caps; font stack unchanged ( system-ui, -apple-system, Segoe UI, Roboto, sans-serif ); every SVG has a child and role="img" . Text is always in the title/muted colors, never in a series color. link-speed-overview-{light,dark}.svg (README headline) viewBox 0 0 1000 560 , fixed pixel layout, stdlib only, byte-deterministic (unchanged rules). Title: Link time saved by llvm-ld, by build mode . Subtitle: vs. stock lld-link (LLVM 23.1.0 payload before the patches) · same runner, interleaved · byte-identical EXE and PDB · at {T} threads , where {T} is the highest thread count measured (4 on the hosted runner). x: four groups in mode order. Group label line 1 (bold, 13px): the chart label from the table; line 2 (muted, 11px): the flags, e.g. -O0 -g · /debug:full /opt:noref,noicf . bars: one per corpus present for that mode at {T} threads, ordered small -> medium -> large, ordinal ramp, centered in the group. thinlto has two bars and a muted note under the group: large not measured . y: % less wall time (paired median) from 0 to nice_ceiling(max * 1.12) ; a zero rule; if any cell is negative the axis extends below zero as today, and the bar hangs below the rule. labels: on every bar cap, bold 13px: +43% ; under it in muted 11px: 1163 -> 656 ms . Whisker: the IQR of the paired speedup (from speedup_percent_q1 to _q3 ). legend (three swatches): small · 64 objects , medium · 512 objects , large · 2048 objects . footer: run {id} · source {sha[:12]} · {cpu}, {cores} cores · Linux, glibc malloc · higher is better . link-speed-<mode>-{light,dark}.svg (one per mode) viewBox 0 0 1000 460 . Title: the chart label, e.g. Debug + PDB . Subtitle line 1: exact flags: objects: clang -O0 -g -gcodeview · link: /debug:full /opt:noref /opt:noicf . Subtitle line 2 (muted): the mode's note from the table (this is how the control and the ThinLTO expectation are stated). three facets side by side, one per corpus in order small, medium, large, each with its own ms axis from 0 to nice_ceiling(max baseline ms in facet * 1.15) , three gridlines labelled in ms ( 1,200 ms ). Facet title: large · 2048 objects . A corpus the mode does not measure keeps its slot and shows, centered and muted, not measured (for thinlto/large : not measured: ThinLTO codegen ). inside a facet: x positions are the thread counts measured for that mode ( 1 , 2 , 4 threads; thinlto has one position). At each position two bars, stock lld (gray) then llvm-ld (blue), 22px wide, 2px gap. Tip labels in muted 11px: 1163 and 656 (unit is on the axis). Above the pair, bold 13px: +43% . Whiskers: IQR of that side's wall samples ( wall_ms_q1..q3 ). facet caption (muted 11px, under the x labels): the CPU and RSS trade at the highest thread count in that facet: at 4 threads: CPU -13% · peak RSS +2.6% . This is the memory disclosure CLAUDE.md asks for, next to the win it paid for. legend (two swatches): stock lld-link (LLVM 23.1.0, before the patches) , llvm-ld ; plus n = 9 paired links per bar, medians; whiskers = interquartile range (n varies per mode). footer: same provenance line as the overview. Both chart kinds must remain legible at ~880px README width (scale 0.88): minimum font size in the SVG is 11px. Dashboard index.html <picture> for every panel: <source media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)" srcset="link-speed-<x>-dark.svg"> and <img src="link-speed-<x>-light.svg" alt="..."> . validate_html_links gains srcset to its loading-references check (remote srcset rejected, local must resolve). Body gets a prefers-color-scheme dark style so the dark SVGs sit on a dark page; still no remote loads. Sections: #overview , then #debug , #release-pdb , #release-nopdb , #thinlto , each with the chart and a short paragraph repeating the flags and note; then #cells table with columns Mode, Corpus, Threads, Runs, Saved % (IQR), llvm-ld ms, Stock ms, CPU, Peak RSS, EXE sha, PDB sha (or none ); then #caveats (thread cap, allocator, platform transfer, ThinLTO scope) and provenance/reproduce as today. README ## Link speed Replace the two images and the history sentence with: one paragraph; the overview <picture> ; a ### By build mode subsection with the four per-mode <picture> blocks in mode order, each preceded by one bold line naming the mode and its flags; then the existing caveat bullets, amended: the thread-cap bullet drops the history reference; a new bullet says ThinLTO is measured on small and medium at the highest thread count only, and why; the data link points at latest.json and the dashboard only. Drop history Remove link-speedup-history.svg , link-speedup-threads.svg , history_panel_svg , threads_panel_svg , history.jsonl , HISTORY_SCHEMA , HISTORY_LIMIT , read_history / read_history_text / merge_history / history_row / history_sort_key / reject_duplicate_history , the --history-in / --initialize-history arguments, and the resolve prior publication step's git show FETCH_HEAD:history.jsonl (the step still records prior_sha for --force-with-lease ). Remove the #history / #threads sections and the README/dashboard/CLAUDE.md text about the history panel and "highest measured thread count" tracking. prepare-branch already clears the branch before staging, so the old files disappear on the next publish; precheck reads only run.source_sha and keeps working across the schema bump. Data and code changes tests/perf/gen_corpus.py MODES dict: id -> {label, cflags, link_flags, pdb, corpora, threads_policy ("all" | "max"), runs, note} ; --mode (default release-pdb ); output layout <out>/<mode>/<profile>/ ; manifest.json gains mode , cflags , link_flags , pdb . The old <out>/<profile> layout is simply not read any more (delete build-perf/corpus/{small,medium,large} locally). --print-matrix --max-threads N [--smoke] [--runs R] [--lto-runs L] prints one mode profile threads runs line per cell (thread list 1 2 4 N deduplicated, or N only for max policy; --smoke restricts every mode to small ). Both workflow loops iterate this output. tests/perf/bench.py Reads <corpus>/manifest.json ; passes /pdb: only when pdb is true; the gate hashes the PDB only when the mode produces one and fails if one side produced a PDB and the other did not ; gate.*.pdb / pdb_bytes are null for no-PDB modes. Factors the statistics into a pure summarize(candidate_samples, baseline_samples) and adds: paired_wall_ratio_q1/q3 and speedup_percent_q1/q3 ( statistics.quantiles(ratios, n=4, method="inclusive") ; requires runs >= 4 ), and wall_ms_q1/q3 on both sides. Adds mode to the JSON. --runs below 4 is rejected when --json is requested: a cell without a spread is not publishable. Interactive runs without --json keep today's behaviour. tools/bench_report.py MODES (ids, labels, flags text, notes; asserted equal to gen_corpus.MODES ids by a test), THEMES = ("light", "dark") , PALETTES . SITE_FILES = .nojekyll , index.html , latest.json , manifest.json , plus link-speed-overview-{theme}.svg and link-speed-{mode}-{theme}.svg for every mode and theme (10 SVGs). FILE_CAPS / MEDIA_TYPES / ROLES / SVG_FILES are derived from the same loop (roles speed-overview-panel-{theme} , speed-mode-panel-{mode}-{theme} ). load_cells : reads mode from each cell; unknown mode or corpus fails; a mode with no cells fails (the file set is fixed, so every panel must have data); cells sort by (mode order, corpus order, threads). LATEST_SCHEMA = "llvm-ld-link-latest-v2" , STATISTICS_VERSION = "paired-interleaved-median-iqr-v1" , MANIFEST_SCHEMA = "...-v2" . latest.json gains a top-level modes list (id, label, cflags, link_flags, pdb, note) and per-cell mode , speedup_percent_q1/q3 , paired_wall_ratio_q1/q3 , candidate.wall_ms_q1/q3 , baseline.wall_ms_q1/q3 ; gate.pdb_sha256 / pdb_bytes become nullable. comparison_key_for includes the per-mode corpora and thread sets. reproduction_command becomes the two-line gen/bench pair for release-pdb/large with --mode . New renderers overview_panel_svg(latest, theme) and mode_panel_svg(latest, mode, theme) replace the two line-chart renderers; draw_frame / nice_ceiling / svg_text are reused; a draw_bar(x, y0, y1, width, color) and draw_whisker are added. .github/workflows/link-benchmark.yml Inputs: runs (default 9) and new lto_runs (default 5); mode: smoke maps to --smoke (every mode, small only, never publishes). Corpus cache: path build-perf/corpus , key corpus-{full|smoke}-{sha256(gen_corpus.py)[:16]}-{clang id} as today (the generator hash changes whenever a mode changes). After generation, du -sh build-perf/corpus goes to the step summary. Budget estimate from the existing 320 MB release-pdb corpus: roughly 800 MB uncompressed for all four modes, well under the shared 10 GB budget after zstd, but it is now the second-largest entry after sccache and must be watched. generate corpora and measure loop over python3 tests/perf/gen_corpus.py --print-matrix --max-threads "$(nproc)" [--smoke] --runs "$RUNS" --lto-runs "$LTO_RUNS" ; measure calls bench.py --corpus build-perf/corpus/$mode/$profile --threads $threads --runs $runs --json "$RUNNER_TEMP/cells/$mode-$profile-t$threads.json" and prints each cell's wall-clock cost to the step summary. Cost budget on the hosted 4-core runner: the current 9 cells take ~1.5 min; the non-LTO modes add ~3 min (debug objects link slowest) and ~0.5 min (no PDB); thinlto small+medium at 5 runs is estimated at 3-8 min. Target: measure under 20 minutes with warm corpora. If thinlto/medium alone exceeds 5 minutes on the runner, drop it to small only in the same PR and say so in the note. A cold corpus build is estimated at 40-50 minutes and only happens when gen_corpus.py or clang changes; the 240-minute job timeout covers it. The header comment's "highest measured thread count" paragraph is rewritten to describe the matrix. tests/test_bench_report.py Synthetic cells for all four modes as bench.py now writes them (including a release-nopdb cell with null PDB fields and thinlto cells for small/medium at t4 only); render passes validate-site ; exactly the new SITE_FILES exist; each mode SVG contains its flags and note; the overview contains large not measured ; no file contains history ; index.html contains <picture> and prefers-color-scheme . Negative tests: a missing mode fails render; a cell with an unknown mode fails; a remote srcset fails validate_html_links ; runs < 4 in a cell fails load_cells . MODES ids equal between gen_corpus.py and bench_report.py . New tests/test_bench_stats.py : bench.summarize on synthetic samples yields the documented median/q1/q3 and speedup fields, and the paired-median identity speedup = 100 * (1 - median ratio) holds. CLAUDE.md ( Published link-speed charts ) Update: the SITE_FILES list and the "adding a file" sentence; remove "the time series lives in history.jsonl (capped at 1000 rows)"; replace "dark palette" with the two-theme statement and the <picture> rule; add the mode matrix pointer ( gen_corpus.MODES , --print-matrix ) to the invariants list; note that corpora now live at build-perf/corpus/<mode>/<profile> in the "Link-speed work" section and that bench.py requires --runs >= 4 for JSON output. BASELINE_REF , the FILES derivation, and the identical-binary guard are unchanged. Acceptance python -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_bench_*.py' passes. Local end-to-end on an idle machine ( uptime load checked first): gen_corpus.py --mode <m> --profile <p> for every matrix cell, bench.py against the local candidate and baseline for every cell (every gate passes, including the no-PDB gate and the ThinLTO gate), bench_report.py render , validate-site . Both themes of every panel are converted to PNG and checked by eye at 880px width for label collisions, whisker legibility, the not measured slots and the negative-bar case (use a synthetic cell for the last one). The PR description records the per-mode measure wall time from a workflow_dispatch smoke run and the corpus size printed to the step summary. The PR is green and merged. After merge, link-benchmark republishes: benchmark-stats holds exactly the new file set (14 files), the README shows the overview and four mode charts in both GitHub themes, the dashboard shows every section, and latest.json has the v2 schema with mode on every cell.
